Cusco · Perú

Q'enqo

A carved channel in an otherwise irregular outcrop

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

A limestone outcrop has been carved into channels, ledges and a passage. Walk around its outer face first: the contrast between rough stone and cut surfaces makes the intervention of Inca masons visible before you enter the more confined space.

Planning your visit

30–50 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

A carved channel in an otherwise irregular outcrop

At the boundary between unworked rock and a cut channel, look across the groove rather than straight down into it. Side light reveals its depth without touching the surface.

History and local experience

Natural limestone sets the bounds of the design here. Rather than assembling an entire structure from blocks, the builders removed stone to shape the outcrop itself.

Walking route

  1. Q'enqo, carretera Cusco–Pisac
  2. From the signed entrance follow the exterior circuit, pause beside the cut channels and use the passage only if the attendant has opened it.
  3. Return by the marked exit.

Before you go

Return by the marked exit.
